nodes.name: When Executed by Parent Workflow
nodes.notes: Entry point when a parent workflow calls this one. Set to passthrough: the calling nodes in the catalog declare no input fields, so whatever the parent emits arrives here unchanged.

nodes.name: Apply 'standard' Handling
nodes.notes: Normalises the routed lead and records which switch arm handled them. Add the 'standard'-specific work here - this is the extension point the parent's switch was built around.

nodes.name: Return Handled Lead
nodes.notes: Returns to the parent's Merge Routed Work node, which appends this arm's items alongside the others. `status` is set for consistency with the Post-Process libs; the branch callers only read the error rail.

### Apply 'standard' Handling

Normalises the items and tags `route: 'standard'`.

🛠 This is where 'standard'-specific logic goes.

Next: Return Handled Lead

### Return Handled Lead

Writes `status`, `handledBy`, `route`, then returns to the parent's Merge Routed Work.

## lib: Process Standard Lead

The 'standard' arm of a parent's **Route by Work Type** switch, for lead. Shipped as a working passthrough so the branch completes end to end; the branch-specific rules are yours to add.

**Called by:** parent templates that reference `lib: Process Standard Lead` in an Execute Workflow or Workflow Tool node.

nodes.name: Note: lib: Process Standard Lead overview

parameters.content:
### Contract

**In:** the lead the switch routed to 'standard'. No fields required.

**Out:** the same items with `route`, `handledBy` and `status` added, appended by the parent's Merge Routed Work node. Callers read only the error rail, so any additional field you add here flows on untouched.

nodes.name: Note: lib: Process Standard Lead contract

parameters.content:
### Credentials setup

**None.** This lib calls nothing external, so it runs as imported.

nodes.name: Note: lib: Process Standard Lead credentials

parameters.content:
### Troubleshooting

**The branch does nothing useful yet.** By design - the parents establish that 'standard' is routed separately, but none of them documents what should happen to it. Put that logic in the Apply 'standard' Handling node.

**Items appear twice after the merge.** The parent's Merge Routed Work is in append mode across all arms; check the switch is not sending the same item down two arms.

nodes.name: Note: lib: Process Standard Lead troubleshooting
